name: Repair-aware IBN
description: Research artefact for the paper Accurate Conflict Detectors Fail at Intent Resolution: Boundary Awareness and Repair-Aware Training in SDN. A learned detector that flags a conflict between two network intents is accurate at detection yet close to useless at resolution: removing the predicate relation that provably resolves the conflict leaves it calling the pair a conflict. This release contains the benchmark, code and per-seed results used to measure that gap and to close it through repair-aware training. Contents Generated intent-conflict benchmark of 480 intent pairs, 240 of them conflicts, with the resolving relation recorded per instance and confounders verified non-causal by rejection sampling. The generator, so the benchmark can be regenerated under any seed. A held-out set of 36 hand-authored intent pairs in operator-style phrasing, never used for training or calibration. Code for the conflict detector, repair-aware training, counterfactual repair search, Integrated Gradients attribution, the faithfulness gate, the hybrid propose-and-verify baselines and the decision-threshold sweep. Per-seed result files backing every number reported in the paper. Leakage and non-causality diagnostic scripts, so the dataset guarantees can be rechecked independently rather than taken on trust. Experiments use two seed protocols: ten seeds with the dataset fixed, and five seeds with the dataset regenerated per seed. Both are named in every reported aggregate.
